item.title: BEML plans to build tunnel-boring machines to cut reliance on China
item.description: The company plans to initially focus on smaller tunnel-boring machines, or TBMs, used in metro rail, hydropower, irrigation and water projects before expanding into larger equipment ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Aryan Gupta BEML Ltd., India’s state-owned defence and engineering company, aims to develop tunnel-boring machines in a bet that the country’s infrastructure boom can support a homegrown effort to replace foreign suppliers. The company plans to initially focus on smaller tunnel-boring machines, or TBMs, used in metro rail, hydropower, irrigation and water projects before expanding into larger equipment, Chairman and Managing Director Shantanu Roy said in an interview. The move is part of India’s broader efforts to reduce import reliance, particularly from China. The South Asian nation is among the biggest users of tunneling machines as it accelerates spending on transportation and underground infrastructure. While China’s recent tightening of export controls on certain categories of construction equipment has underscored India’s dependence on overseas suppliers, Roy said BEML’s plans were already in motion. “We have done our homework,” Roy said, adding “we are ready with a plan.” BEML, which makes military and mining vehicles and rail cars, is onboarding a global consultant to support the effort to eventually gain self-reliance. Rather than targeting the largest and most technically demanding machines from the outset, BEML plans to begin with TBMs between 3.5 meters and 6.5 meters in diameter — commonly used in urban transit and utility projects and represent a smaller segment of the market.Bullet TrainTBMs excavating the Mumbai section of India’s first bullet-train line have cutter-heads about 13.6 meters in diameter and were manufactured by Germany’s Herrenknecht AG at its China facility.  BEML aims to develop proprietary technology instead of assembling imported kits, Roy said. “It will be an indigenous technology,” he said. “The IP will be Indian.” Whether that ambition translates into a commercially viable domestic industry remains to be seen. India has repeatedly sought to reduce dependence on Chinese supply chains in strategically important sectors, only to find that developing local manufacturing ecosystems takes longer than building assembly capacity.  Rare-earth magnets are a recent example. After Beijing restricted exports of rare-materials and technologies, New Delhi approved a 72.8 billion rupee ($820 million) program aimed at establishing 6,000 tons of annual permanent-magnet capacity. Yet India was still importing all of its high-performance neodymium magnets as of July because it lacked industrial-scale facilities to convert rare-earth materials into metals, alloys and finished magnets, according to the Ministry of Heavy Industries. The country’s efforts at solar manufacturing also paint a similar picture. While India has built one of the world’s largest solar-module manufacturing industries, it remains heavily reliant on imports for key upstream materials and equipment, according to the government’s policy think-tank and industry studies.Tunneling InvestmentsBEML sees the market for tunneling machinery growing as India increases investments in underground infrastructure. Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari has said the country aims to invest up to $9.6 billion in tunneling projects over the next five years, while policymakers have encouraged local manufacturing of construction equipment. Demand is also being driven by strategic road and railway projects across India’s Himalayan frontier with China, where difficult terrain often requires extensive tunneling. Roy estimates India’s TBM market could expand about 12% annually over the next seven to eight years, roughly twice the pace of the global market. Still, the company’s ambitions remain in their early stages. BEML expects it would take about 22 months to deliver its first machine after winning a contract. “Gradually we will move on to the next level,” Roy said.

item.title: Codelco, Adani Group sign agreement for copper exploration project
item.description: Adani would provide financing for the project, which could offer long-term supply for its smelting complex in Mundra, India, Codelco said in a statement ...
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Chile's state-run copper producer Codelco said on Wednesday it has signed a agreement with India's Adani Group to develop the Kaburkaala copper exploration project in Chile's northern region of Antofagasta.Adani would provide financing for the project, which could offer long-term supply for its smelting complex in Mundra, India, Codelco said in a statement.The two companies agreed last year to a partnership and evaluated a number of potential Codelco copper projects before Adani selected Kaburkaala for exploration.India relies on copper imports to address shortfalls and meet the robust demand in the world's fastest-growing major economy and has been seeking to shore up its supply with investments overseas.The agreement was signed between Codelco and Kutch Copper Limited, part of Adani Group.

item.title: Stock Market LIVE: Sensex flat at pre-open, Nifty around 25,200; Asian markets advance
item.description: The GIFT Nifty indicated a positive open for the Nifty50 index. Asian markets were trading higher in early deals ...
item.dc:creator: SI Reporter
item.content:encoded: Sensex Today | Stock Market LIVE Updates, Thursday, Nov 12, 2026:  At pre-open, the Nifty50 and the Sensex were trading on muted note with a negative bias as traders assessed global cues.  Most Asia-Pacific markets were trading higher in early trade on Thursday, mirroring overnight moves on Wall Street. Japan’s Nikkei 225 and South Korea’s Kospi rose 0.72 per cent and 0.67 per cent, respectively. Meanwhile, the Hang Seng fell 1.27 per cent.  Overnight, the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 settled 0.49 per cent and 1.31 per cent higher, respectively. The Nasdaq Composite ended 1.60 per cent higher.  In the after-market, Nvidia share price slumped 7 per cent after news reports said that the board may prepare to oust CEO Jensen Huang.  Brent crude erased gains on Thursday morning. In the previous session, oil prices rose 1 per cent after Iran said it would keep its nuclear material reserve — the primary bone of contention between Tehran and Washington. The January futures were quoted at $91.93 per barrel on the Intercontinental Exchange, down 0.77 per cent.  Gold and silver futures fell 0.29 per cent and 0.74 per cent, respectively.  Q2 Results TodayAction Construction Equipment, Alkem Laboratories, Amber Enterprises India, Astra Microwave Products, Automotive Axles, Avalon Technologies, Bharat Dynamics, Bondada Engineering, Caplin Point Laboratories, Dilip Buildcon, Dollar Industries, EIH, Elevate Campuses, EMS, Ethos, Fiem Industries, Hindustan Aeronautics, Hinduja Global Solutions, Vodafone Idea, IFCI, Indian Railway Catering & Tourism Corporation (IRCTC), Kennametal India, Kesoram Industries, Landmark Cars, Manappuram Finance, Man Industries (India), NMDC, NMDC Steel, Oil India, Ola Electric Mobility, Oswal Pumps, Page Industries, Procter & Gamble Hygiene & Health Care, Hitachi Energy India, Premier Explosives, Rane Holdings, Rashtriya Chemicals & Fertilizers (RCF), Religare Enterprises, Reliance Power, Sharda Motor Industries, S.P. Apparels, TARC, Tarsons Products, TD Power Systems, Techno Electric & Engineering Company, Travel Food Services, Uflex will release their results on Wednesday.

item.title: Nvidia preparing to oust Jensen Huang after multiple extramarital affairs
item.description: Nvidia Corp.’s board is preparing to oust Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang after multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman who is reportedly suspected of being a Chinese spy, the ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Lynn Doan Nvidia Corp.’s board is preparing to oust Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang after multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman who is reportedly suspected of being a Chinese spy, the Wall Street Journal said Wednesday. ALSO READ: Huang said to have had relationship with Nvidia exec who reports to him The board was preparing to meet as soon as Wednesday to decide Huang’s fate at the company, the Journal reported, citing unidentified people familiar with the matter. ALSO READ: Alice Huang, alleged Chinese spy in Nvidia scandal, currently in Beijing Nvidia’s board has been facing a succession crisis since Sunday when Huang admitted that he’d had an affair with Alice Huang, who is reportedly suspected of spying on behalf of China. The disclosure shined a light on Nvidia’s lack of a succession plan for Huang and reinforced how inseparable the 63-year-old CEO is from the company and its success. Huang’s potential exit would reverberate far beyond the company’s operations, and not just because Nvidia is the dominant maker of chips at the heart of the AI boom. Huang is a consummate dealmaker and has used the company’s vast resources to invest in the AI supply chain and a variety of startups. He’s also a top evangelist for the AI revolution itself, downplaying fears about the risks to humanity and talking up the benefits. Nvidia didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment. Shares of Nvidia dropped 8% in extended trading to $159.95 at about 5:35 p.m. New York time. That’s after closing at $173.73 on Wednesday. Earlier on Wednesday, the New York Times reported that Huang had also had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, citing unidentified people who worked at the company. Huang and Powell were captured on video being affectionate at a hotel in San Jose, California, during an Nvidia conference in March, according to the Times. Powell didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.  On Sunday, Huang admitted to having an affair with Alice Huang, who was an executive at Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based firm that was spun out of a Chinese gaming enterprise. That data center company, which is Nvidia’s largest Southeast Asian customer, has been under US investigation for months related to potential chip smuggling, Bloomberg has reported. Megaspeed and Nvidia have denied wrongdoing. Beijing has dismissed allegations that it spied on Huang.
